context: Request: real estate matters with an assignment-consent requirement on the deal itself (lease, purchase agreement or property interest), with the executed documents. Rubric: seven matters 1017-00009 (Aurelius lease), 1026-00004 (Linden PSA), 1027-00004 (Pellegrino hotel PSA), 1031-00004 (MTDC loan / escrow), 1036-00004 (Fairwater portfolio), 1043-00002 (Ironhaven land PSAs), 1043-00003 (Ironhaven construction financing), an executed document for each, plus a precision criterion (15 criteria).

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.why: The store-wide scan's result was viewed only through its first 200 of about 7,900 hits, and the tighter rerun only through a fixed candidate list, so two needed matters never appeared; it did not page through the saved hits.
first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) [21] said candidates were listed from a truncated, noisy output, without naming any missing matter.

other_errors.why: It read one needed matter's purchase agreement and another's construction-contract assignment at [68]-[77] and listed a third at [54]-[55], but the answer excludes all three; no review questioned these exclusions.

The answer asserts three matters outside the set (two asset-purchase lease assignments and an entity-interest transfer read at [30]-[80]); after the reviews it relabelled one as borderline but kept all three.
other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) [51], [102] and [111] named these matters as possibly not deal-level consents.

divergence: All three runs failed, each with a different first error but the same overall pattern: incomplete coverage of the seven needed matters plus over-inclusion of asset-purchase deals whose leases were assigned. T0 surfaced all seven by file name but never listed one (surfaced-not-opened) and excluded two it read as lender-consent comparators, one of which the review had itself suggested was a lender-consent hit. T1 surfaced all seven but scanned only a hardcoded candidate list that dropped three (over-narrow-filter). T2 viewed its scans only through truncated or candidate-filtered output and never saw two (search-miss). Reviews flagged these only generically; in T2 the reviews also pushed to drop a needed portfolio matter, which the agent kept as borderline.
